title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, tenant Union Ties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, tenant Union Ties] Should my campaign be linked to the local tenant union?

Real talk: Absolutely. The tenant union is the backbone of working-class power in the city. Their struggle is your struggle, and your campaign should be a vehicle for their demands. When you win, you’re not just a politician; you’re an extension of their movement inside the government. Use your platform to amplify their strikes and their demands for universal rent control and the right to counsel in eviction court.

title: Karl Organizing: Security for Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security for Funds] Who should be in charge of the money?

Never leave the bag with just one person. Elect a committee of three people who have to sign off on any major spending and who are all accountable to the general membership. This prevents burnout, stops bad actors from disappearing with the loot, and ensures that every spending decision reflects the will of the collective. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: cloud Storage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: cloud Storage] Give me the short version: Is it okay to store my organizing notes on iCloud?

No. Apple has the keys and they will hand them over. Use an encrypted note-taking app like Standard Notes or just keep them in an encrypted local file. If it’s in the cloud, it’s on someone else’s computer, and that someone else is a billionaire who doesn't care about your revolution. Keep your plans on hardware you control. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, the Sheriff's Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, the Sheriff's Office] Is it worth running for Sheriff to abolish the position?

Look, Running for Sheriff is about immediate harm reduction and throwing a wrench in the deportation machine. You can refuse to cooperate with ICE, stop the eviction crews from throwing families on the street, and end the barbaric practice of cash bail in your county. We want the office gone, but until it is, we need a comrade holding the keys who refuses to turn them against the working class. Use the power to de-escalate, demilitarize, and defend the vulnerable.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: avoiding Sectarianism
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: avoiding Sectarianism] Give me the short version: There is a group we have beef with, but they agree with us on this campaign. Do we work with them?

I don't care if you hate their stickers or their favorite dead theorist. If they are willing to put boots on the pavement to stop an eviction or challenge a billionaire, they are a temporary comrade. Keep the internal beef for the pub and keep your eyes on the ruling class's throat; we don't have the luxury of purity tests when the rent is due.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustainer Programs] Can you explain: is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?

Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: crowd Logistics] Give me the short version: How do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Let me break it down: Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] A friend asked me: 'Is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database.

title: Karl Organizing: Tool Libraries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tool Libraries] A friend asked me: 'How do we stop people from stealing or breaking the tools in our sharing library?' What do I tell them?

Trust is our currency, but a simple checkout sheet and a 'how-to' guide for expensive gear keeps things running smooth. If someone breaks a drill, they don't get punished; we just ask them to help the crew learn how to fix it. People take care of things when they realize the tool belongs to the whole community, not some faceless corporation. Keep a small fund for repairs by asking comrades to chip in a few bucks when they can.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, building a Platform
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, building a Platform] What should be at the top of my local campaign platform?

Here's how it works: Housing as a human right, period. If you aren't talking about rent control, social housing, and an end to homelessness, you aren't serious about helping the working class. Add in a demand for robust public transit and a promise to tax the big local businesses to pay for it all. Keep the language simple and the promises bold so the average person knows exactly whose side you are on from the jump.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: building Trust] Give me the short version: How do we trust people we have never worked with before?

Here's the thing: Trust is built through sweat and shared risk, not long meetings and promises. Start with a small, low-stakes action like a joint flyer drop or a community meal to see who actually shows up when it is raining. If they do the work, they are in; if they just want to talk in circles while you're trying to organize, keep them at arm's length.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: handling Incumbents
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: handling Incumbents] Give me the short version: My opponent has been in office for 20 years. How do I beat that?

Use their longevity as an indictment of the status quo. If things are a mess after two decades of their leadership, why should anyone give them another four years? Focus on the stagnation and the cozy relationships they’ve built with the local elite over those years. Frame yourself as the fresh air and the voice of a new generation that refuses to accept the same old failures.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] How should our defense group talk to each other during an emergency?

Stop using SMS or Facebook groups immediately because those are open books for the state. Stick to Signal with disappearing messages turned on and verify the safety numbers of every comrade in your circle. During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: the Sheriff's Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: the Sheriff's Office] Give me the short version: Is it worth running for Sheriff to abolish the position?

Running for Sheriff is about immediate harm reduction and throwing a wrench in the deportation machine. You can refuse to cooperate with ICE, stop the eviction crews from throwing families on the street, and end the barbaric practice of cash bail in your county. We want the office gone, but until it is, we need a comrade holding the keys who refuses to turn them against the working class. Use the power to de-escalate, demilitarize, and defend the vulnerable.

title: Karl Organizing: Shared Demands
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Shared Demands] A friend asked me: 'How do we pick what to fight for when every group in the room wants something different?' What do I tell them?

Find the one demand that hits the bosses hardest and lifts the floor for every person in that room. Don't get bogged down in a laundry list of fifty niche items; pick three demands that everyone can scream at a rally without checking a script. Focus on what unites your material interests—like rent caps or higher wages—not your subcultural identities. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, small Group Value] Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

Here's how it works: A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: Organizing 'Scab' Neighbors
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Organizing 'Scab' Neighbors] One neighbor is a suck-up to the landlord and tells them everything we do. What do we do?

Here's the thing: Don't waste energy attacking them, but freeze them out of the strategy meetings. Continue winning improvements for the whole building; when that neighbor sees their own rent stay flat or their repairs get done because of the union's work, their loyalty to the parasite will crumble. Success is the best recruitment tool for the skeptical and the scared.

title: Karl Organizing: Reconnaissance
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Reconnaissance] Should we check out the protest location a few days before?

You wouldn't walk into a boss's office without a plan, so don't hit the streets blind. Scout the area for surveillance cameras, narrow chokepoints, and multiple escape routes before the big day. Knowing where the private security hides and where the shadows are deep gives us the tactical edge we need to keep our people safe and the ruling class on their toes. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Long-term Planning] A friend asked me: 'How do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: School board organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[School board organizing] How do I organize around my school board?

Let me break it down: Show up to meetings — most have five people in the audience, so twenty organized parents is a movement. Read the agenda in advance. Build a parent-teacher coalition. Run candidates if the board won't listen. School boards control billions and shape kids' lives; the far right knows this, and so should we.

title: Karl Organizing: Ballot Access Laws
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ballot Access Laws] Can you explain: the state just passed new laws making it harder for independents to run. What now?

Let me break it down: They’re changing the rules because they’re terrified of us. We treat their hurdles as a mobilization opportunity—turn the signature gathering into a massive rally and a public education campaign about their voter suppression. File the lawsuits if you have to, but focus on building a movement so large that their paperwork tricks can't stop the tide. We don't ask for permission to represent our people; we take it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: clinic Defense] Give me the short version: What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] What happens if one of us gets picked up by the cops?

Here's how it works: Never leave a comrade behind in the system's meat-grinder. Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker and make sure everyone knows to call it the second a snatch squad moves in. Pool resources for a bail fund ahead of time so we can get our people out of those cages and back to the front lines where they belong.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: disability Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: disability Accessibility] Give me the short version: How do we make our mutual aid events more accessible for disabled comrades?

Here's how it works: Start by asking disabled folks what they need instead of guessing and getting it wrong. Ensure every meeting spot has ramps and sensory-friendly spaces, and always provide captions or ASL if you're doing a presentation. Mutual aid that ignores the most marginalized among us isn't mutual—it's just a club for the able-bodied. Build accessibility into the foundation of your group so no one has to 'request' entry to their own community.

title: Karl Organizing: Transportation Networks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transportation Networks] Can you explain: how can we help neighbors who don't have cars get to grocery stores or doctors?

Start a dispatch thread where comrades with vehicles can post their availability for the week. If you're going to the store anyway, check the list and see which neighbor needs a ride or a delivery. We can bypass the predatory ride-share apps by simply looking out for each other and pooling our gas money. It's about making sure no one is trapped in their home just because they can't afford a mechanic.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, anti-Harassment Tactics] How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Real talk: Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Member Dues] A friend asked me: 'How do we get people to pay dues every month?' What do I tell them?

Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: eviction Defense] Give me the short version: How do we stop a neighbor from being evicted?

Look, When the sheriff shows up, you need a crowd of neighbors blocking the doors and the moving trucks. Organize a phone tree to flood the landlord's office with calls and let them know that an eviction will be more expensive and public than just letting the tenant stay. Move their furniture back in if they try to toss it. Housing is a right, and we defend it with our collective physical presence.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] Should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Disability Accessibility

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, winning Small
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, winning Small] Is it okay to accept a small victory even if it's not everything we wanted?

Real talk: Take the win, bank the momentum, and immediately demand the rest. A small victory proves to your neighbors that fighting back actually works and gets them ready for the next, bigger round. Never call it a day; use every concession from the bosses as a stepping stone to take even more power away from them tomorrow.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, scaling Up
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, scaling Up] How do we grow from a local coalition to something bigger?

Find coalitions in the next town over that are fighting the same boss or the same landlord and link your demands. You don't need a massive national headquarters; you need a network of local groups that can strike or protest simultaneously to paralyze the system. Power is built from the bottom up, one block and one shop floor at a time, until the whole structure shakes.

title: Karl Organizing: Food distribution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food distribution] What's the best way to run a food distribution?

Let me break it down: Partner with food banks for supply — they throw away mountains of good food. Pick a consistent time and place so people can rely on it. No ID, no questions, no sermons. Bag staples people actually cook with. And recruit from the community you're serving — the distribution should be run by neighbors, not outsiders.

title: Karl Organizing: Tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tactical Diversity] Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Here's how it works: Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: city Council motivation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: city Council motivation] Give me the short version: Why should I run for city council when the real power is in DC?

Here's the thing: The feds won't stop your landlord from hiking the rent, but a council vote can. We're seizing the levers that actually touch people’s lives every single morning—the cops, the zoning, and the water bills. Grab a clipboard, talk to the people at the bus stop, and let’s start making the bosses sweat where they actually live. Don't wait for a savior from the capital when you can be the shield for your own block right now.

title: Karl Organizing: Photo Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Photo Policy] Can I take pictures of the protest for social media?

Take all the photos of the cops and the banners you want, but never, ever show a comrade's face, tattoos, or unique clothing. The ruling class uses social media as a giant facial recognition database to target activists after the fact. Use blur apps or emojis to cover faces before you post anything, because a 'cool' photo isn't worth a friend's freedom. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Fridge Startup] How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skill-sharing for Cash] How can we raise money using our own talents?

Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Free clinic basics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free clinic basics] How do we start a free health clinic?

Find volunteer medical professionals first — nurses, EMTs, med students. Partner with an existing community space. Start small: blood pressure checks, wound care, Narcan distribution. Handle the legal side — liability waivers, a sponsoring nonprofit. Grow services as trust grows. Healthcare is a right; build the proof.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, verification
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, verification] How do we avoid acting on fake reports of police activity?

Real talk: Never share a report you haven't personally verified or heard from a trusted scout on the ground. Use a 'trusted source' protocol where two different people have to confirm the sighting before the alert goes out to the whole network. False alarms burn people out and make the network look unreliable. Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast when it comes to reporting state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Public Messaging] How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Here's the thing: Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining the Work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining the Work] A friend asked me: 'I'm exhausted and feel like I'm burning out. How do I keep going?' What do I tell them?

Take a damn break and let the rest of the collective carry the load for a while. Mutual aid isn't a solo performance; it's a relay race where we pass the baton when our legs get heavy. If you burn yourself out, you're no good to the movement or your neighbors, so go rest and recharge. We're in this for the long haul, and that means pacing ourselves so we can see the revolution through to the end.

title: Karl Organizing: Media Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Media Strategy] How do we get the local news to care about our building?

Here's the thing: Journalists love a visual story of David vs. Goliath. Invite them to a 'tour of horrors' through your building to see the rot firsthand. Have a spokesperson ready with a punchy quote about how the landlord lives in a mansion while you live with rats. The goal is to make the landlord's name synonymous with 'slumlord' in every Google search of their business.

title: Karl Organizing: School Board tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[School Board tactics] What can a leftist actually do on a school board?

You stop the privatization ghouls from gutting the classrooms to fund their charter school scams. Fight for universal free meals and kick the cops out of the hallways so kids can actually learn without being treated like prisoners. Use that seat to protect teachers' unions and ensure history is taught as a struggle for the people, not a fairytale for the billionaires. It’s the front line against the right-wing attempt to colonize our children's futures. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Sectarianism
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Avoiding Sectarianism] A friend asked me: 'There is a group we have beef with, but they agree with us on this campaign. Do we work with them?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: I don't care if you hate their stickers or their favorite dead theorist. If they are willing to put boots on the pavement to stop an eviction or challenge a billionaire, they are a temporary comrade. title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: direct Action Support] Give me the short version: How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.

title: Karl Organizing: Red Lines
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Red Lines] How do we know when a compromise is actually a sell-out?

Here's the thing: If the deal helps the bosses more than the workers, or if it throws one part of your coalition under the bus to save the rest, it’s a sell-out. Never trade the rights of one group for a tiny raise for another; that’s how the ruling class divides us. A real win leaves your coalition stronger and more united for the next fight, not fractured and suspicious.

title: Karl Organizing: Coalition building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Coalition building] How do I get different groups to work together?

Let me break it down: Start with a shared, winnable demand — not ideology. The tenants, the union, the church group don't need to agree on everything; they need to agree on what they're fighting for THIS month. Write it down. Assign real responsibilities. And handle conflicts early and directly — coalitions die from unspoken resentments, not disagreements.

title: Karl Organizing: Workplace Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Workplace Safety] My boss is ignoring safety rules. How do we force a change?

Karl's answer: Document every violation with photos and dates, and have your coworkers do the same. Present the list to management as a collective demand and refuse to perform the most dangerous tasks until the issues are fixed. If they retaliate, you take the evidence to the public and the labor board together.

title: Karl Organizing: Elderly Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Elderly Care] How do we make sure the seniors in our building aren't being forgotten?

Do a door-knock every Sunday just to check in and see if they need help with groceries, light bulbs, or tech issues. Many of our elders are isolated by a society that only values people who are currently being exploited for profit. Listen to their stories—they've seen more than you and usually have the best advice for surviving the long haul. A simple check-in can be the difference between someone thriving or suffering in silence.

title: Karl Organizing: Sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sliding Scales] A friend asked me: 'How do we implement a sliding scale for events?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone zaps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone zaps] How do I organize a phone zap?

Real talk: Pick a target with a public number: a landlord, a boss, a politician. Write a 30-second script so callers know exactly what to say. Set a time window and blast it out. The goal isn't persuasion — it's demonstrating that an organized constituency is watching. Fifty calls in an hour gets attention.

Focus on what unites your material interests—like rent caps or higher wages—not your subcultural identities. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowdfunding Platforms] Can you explain: which website should we use to raise money online?

Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: kettling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: kettling] Give me the short version: What should we do if the police box us in from all sides?

Here's the thing: Don't panic—that's exactly what they want. Keep the crowd calm, look for weak points in their line, and start filming immediately to document that they've trapped you without an exit. Kettling is a move used by cowards to manufacture a reason for mass arrests, so stay close to your comrades and keep your spirits high.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?

Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. Bring coffee, bring music, and bring a loud megaphone to let the landlord know the whole neighborhood is watching their cruelty. While you're holding the line, have your legal team file every emergency motion possible to gum up the works. We don't let our people get thrown to the curb while billionaires' apartments sit empty and rotting. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Volunteer Management] How do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?

Here's the thing: Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive.

title: Karl Organizing: Time Bank Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Time Bank Value] Can you explain: in a time bank, is an hour of plumbing worth more than an hour of childcare?

Absolutely not. In our world, an hour of a human being's life is equal regardless of the task they're performing. The capitalists want us to believe some labor is 'unskilled' so they can pay us pennies, but we know better. Whether you're fixing a pipe or watching a comrade's kid so they can organize, you're contributing to our collective survival. We value the person, not the market price of their sweat.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying Officers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying Officers] An officer is being aggressive and doesn't have a badge visible. What do I do?

Film them and demand their name and badge number, but don't get close enough for them to grab you. If they refuse to identify, document their physical description and any markings on their gear. These goons hide their identities because they know they're doing wrong; we'll use your footage to unmask them later. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Undercover Cops
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Undercover Cops] How can we spot a cop trying to blend into the crowd?

Watch for the person trying to push the group into dangerous, unplanned actions or asking way too many questions about who's in charge. If your gut says someone is a plant, move away and quietly alert your trusted crew without starting a panic. We stay safe by trusting our people and ignoring the loudmouths looking for a fight.
